title: Concept knowledge base: a wiki we can manage, rank and feed to agents
description:
Ryan 2026-11-03. Curation is speeding up, so mined concepts and the wiki will grow fast. Concept pages start thin but link to References. Goals: people can create and edit concepts; machines never step on them; concepts are ranked in several ways during knowledge runs; sections track key concepts; agents get graph-based context about their section; the public wiki gets fun, honest views; a site chooses who may edit its wiki.

Measured on Machines on Machines 2026-11-03 (read only):
- 2,755 current concept nodes, 7,662 superseded. 18,292 relations, read in about a minute.
- 1,428 accepted References. None has curationSectionId.
- Reference to concept: 3,366 unreviewed suggested related_to links (vector suggestions, scores as low as 0.19), 13 mentions. 408 mentions go from Items to concepts.
- Links touching accepted References reach only 81 distinct concepts, and two concepts hold 518 of them (335 and 183). So the graph is thin and hub-heavy today; ranking it now would mostly rank noise. Epic 'Raw material' comes first.
- No authority scores are set, though `papyrus knowledge ontology recompute-authority` exists.

Technology decision: no graph database. The knowledge run is a 4 vCPU, 16 GB Fargate task, and this graph fits in memory by a wide margin. Compute in Python during the run, publish JSON and derived fields. S3 Vectors concept cards already exist for sparse concepts.

Already filed under PPY-aab37e and part of this: PPY-891a3f (machines only create concepts), PPY-bbec59 (section lists and basic cards), PPY-b69b15 (automatic concepts experiment, now the lower tier). Decided rules: machines get or create; only derived numbers update; same thing is one node with aliases, found the same means merge, related or unsure means two nodes with a noted link; a typed link plus a note is what a fact is for now; a person's list outranks automatic suggestions.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Correction to the measurements above: 'accepted' here does not mean an editor accepted them. About 56 of the 1,428 were a person's decision; 1,341 are a bulk 'trusted import' from May. See PPY-94eef8.
